verdicts.title: Unsatisfiable CNF Formulas need many Conflicts
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A pair of clauses in a CNF formula constitutes a conflict if there is a variable that occurs positively in one clause and negatively in the other. A CNF formula without any conflicts is satisfiable. The Lovasz Local Lemma implies that a k-CNF formula is satisfiable if each clause conflicts with at most 2^k/e-1 clauses. It does not, however, give any good bound on how many conflicts an unsatisfiable formula has globally. We show here that every unsatisfiable k-CNF formula requires 2.69^k conflict
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns lower/upper bounds on the number of conflicts in unsatisfiable k-CNF formulas, not Frege proof depth or any algebraic-topological local index. It shares the CNF vocabulary but does not interact with the specific claim about local_index(φ) versus d(φ).

verdicts.title: On the Satisfaction Probabilities of $k$-CNF Formulas
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The satisfaction probability Pr[$φ$] := Pr$_{β:vars(φ) \to \{0,1\}}[β\models φ]$ of a propositional formula $φ$ is the likelihood that a random assignment $β$ makes the formula true. We study the complexity of the problem $k$SAT-Pr$_{>p}$ = {$φ$ is a $k$CNF formula | Pr[$φ$] > p} for fixed $k$ and $p$. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns the complexity of deciding satisfaction probability thresholds for k-CNF formulas (a trichotomy in AC^0/NL/NP), with no mention of Frege proof depth, fundamental groups, or local indices from algebraic topology. The 'locality properties' discussed refer to bounded-size subsets of clauses determined by k and p, not to topological local indices.
